<objective>
Re-skin the dashboard shell, the venue switcher and the three venue pages plus the venue form onto the
Cena design system, at the 44px touch floor, and wire the four venue copy rows so no user-visible string
remains outside the copy deck.

Purpose: SC3 names eight surfaces. This plan covers four of them — dashboard, venue create, venue edit,
venue switcher. It is the group with the most source-structural tests pointed at it: one walks the
TypeScript AST of the dashboard layout to prove the create-venue call to action has no conditional
ancestor, another asserts the file-tree shape under the route group, and a third asserts the venue page's
gate coverage. None of them cares about a class; all of them care about shape.

Output: nine re-skinned files, the venue copy wired, all glyphs on the `Icon` wrapper.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It is one half of SC3's owner surfaces.

**The primitives already carry the visual change.** These nine files change layout, spacing and
composition only.
</objective>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">A visual pass over the dashboard shell, the venue switcher and the three venue pages. No action, query, route or authorization boundary changes; the one block that would be irreversible to get wrong — the documented staff-and-device gate — is not touched at all, and a `git diff` gate asserts it. Wiring the four venue copy rows replaces inline strings with references to rows that already exist. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Layout, spacing and glyph routing only.

    **`app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`.** Apply the Cena shell: the sidebar and nav on the sunken surface, the
    content region on paper, 24px section padding, 32px page margins at desktop widths, and a mobile-first
    stack that collapses the sidebar rather than shrinking it. Sidebar chrome resolves through the sidebar
    semantic tokens, which plan 01.1-05 already re-pointed at the Cena ramp — do not add colour classes here.

    **Do not wrap the create-venue link in any conditional, ternary or logical-and — not even for layout.**
    A source-structural test parses this file with the TypeScript compiler and walks that element's
    ancestors, and its table already covers two call sites precisely because this defect shipped twice.
    If the new layout wants the link inside a wrapper, the wrapper must be unconditional. Keep the route
    constant imported from `@/lib/venue-routes`; the same test asserts the import.

    **Do not touch the documented staff-and-device gate block.** It is an access-control boundary carrying
    its own rationale comment, and this phase changes no access-control logic.

    **Keep this file a Server Component.** It performs a Supabase read. If the new design wants a tooltip
    or a hover state anywhere in the shell, extract that leaf into its own client component — the
    server-then-client split already used by the venue switcher is the pattern to follow, and
    `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` names it explicitly as the sanctioned approach.

    **`components/dashboard-nav.tsx`.** Nav rows at the Label role, ink-body by default, with the active
    row taking the accent — one of the few places accent is permitted, alongside the single primary call to
    action, active chips and filters, the selected variant row, the "Clear filters" link and the focus ring.
    Nav rows are interactive: each needs a 44px hit area, achieved by raising the row height rather than
    only its padding. Keep it a Server Component. Route its four glyphs through the `Icon` wrapper.

    **`app/(dashboard)/error.tsx`.** Re-skin the boundary using the re-skinned Card and Button. Do not move
    or rename the file — a test asserts the route group's file-tree shape. Its copy is the generic error
    contract row; do not change it.
  </action>

  <name>Task 2: Re-skin the venue switcher across its server/client split</name>
  <files>app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx, app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx</files>
  <read_first>
    - `app/(dashboard)/components/VenueSwitcher.tsx` in full — the server half, which performs the Supabase read and returns nothing below two venues
    - `app/(dashboard)/components/venue-switcher-menu.tsx` in full — the client half, which imports two glyphs directly and renders the dropdown
    - `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` as re-skinned by plan 01.1-08 — the twenty slots and the 44px row height now inherited
    - `components/ui/icon.tsx` (plan 01.1-07)
    - `lib/copy.ts` — the venue copy rows, in case the switcher's empty affordance needs one
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-PATTERNS.md` § "Server/client split" — this pair is named as *the* pattern to follow
  </read_first>
  <action>
    Layout, spacing and glyph routing only, and the split stays exactly where it is.

    **`VenueSwitcher.tsx` stays a Server Component** and keeps its Supabase read. Do not add the
    client-boundary directive, do not add a hover or tooltip behaviour here, and do not move the read into
    the client half. This pair is the repo's reference example of how to add interactivity during a
    re-skin, and inverting it would move a database read into the browser.

    **`venue-switcher-menu.tsx`** carries the interaction and stays a client component. Give the trigger a
    44px hit area and a truncating single-line venue name so a long name cannot widen the nav or wrap the
    chrome. Give the dropdown its own scroll container with a bounded height, so a long venue list scrolls
    inside the menu rather than growing past a 320px viewport. Menu rows already inherit the 44px height
    from the re-skinned dropdown primitive — verify none is overridden down here.

    Route both of this file's glyphs through the `Icon` wrapper so they draw at 1.75, keeping their
    existing size classes.

    **Do not change the below-two-venues behaviour.** The server half deliberately renders nothing when the
    owner has fewer than two venues. That interacts with a known Phase 01 defect — the switcher is stale
    immediately after a venue is created, so on the one-to-two transition the control fails to appear at
    all — but that defect is fixed in plan 01.1-13, in the action rather than in this component. Changing
    the threshold here would mask it.
  </action>
  <verify>

  </verify>

  <action>
    Layout, spacing, glyph routing, and one copy wiring change.

    **The three venue pages.** Apply the Cena card rhythm: 16px card padding, 24px section breaks, page
    titles at the Display role in `--font-serif`, card titles at Heading in `--font-serif`, body copy at
    Body. Mobile-first, single-column at 320px. The zero-venue state renders the create-first heading and
    body from the copy deck; the has-venues state renders the list. Do not gate the create-venue
    affordance on the list being empty — that is the defect class the ancestor-walking test guards, and it
    has shipped twice.

    **`components/venue-form.tsx` — keep both native select controls.** The registry's select is a styled
    listbox; the native control opens the OS picker, which is strictly better one-handed and is what SC3
    argues for. Swapping it would also break the existing test's reads of the default-language element's
    options collection, changing an existing test's meaning. Style the native controls with the Cena input
    treatment — control-border boundary, paper background, Body role, 44px minimum height — and leave their
    markup as native elements. Do not disturb the controlled-select workaround the comment near line 82
    documents.

    **Wire the four venue copy rows.** The heading and body props currently carry hardcoded string defaults;
    replace those defaults with reads from the copy deck. Those four were the last user-visible strings
    living outside `lib/copy.ts`, and plan 01.1-03 gave each a Copywriting Contract row, so the deck's
    house rule now holds without exception. Change no wording — wire the existing strings.

    **Do not fix the language-checkbox defect here.** The disabled-last-language block is a known Phase 01
    blocker, and it is fixed in plan 01.1-13 together with its regression test, deliberately after this
    re-skin so that a red in the next wave has exactly one suspect. Leave the block as it is, including the
    disabled flag, which an existing test asserts under its own rationale — the refusal is meant to be
    visible rather than a dead click.

    Route the form's glyph through the `Icon` wrapper.

    Run `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` after each edit to this file rather than once at the end.
  </action>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale. The ASVS V4 chapter named in the register below is an out-of-scope-by-contract marker, not a review target — this plan re-skins around the staff-and-device gate without reviewing it, which is why the gate asserts non-change rather than correctness.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| authenticated owner → dashboard route group | The layout carries a documented staff-and-device access gate that decides what an authenticated party may reach. |
| Server Component → browser | `VenueSwitcher.tsx` and the layout perform Supabase reads; pushing either client-side would move a database read into the browser. |
| owner input → venue form | The form's native selects and language checkboxes are the input surface for `createVenue`. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-08 | Elevation of Privilege | The documented staff-and-device gate block altered during the re-skin | high | mitigate | ASVS V4 is out of scope for this phase by contract: the block is not touched, and a `git diff` gate asserts no change inside it. Changes are limited to layout, spacing and glyph routing. |
| T-01.1-30 | Elevation of Privilege | The layout or `VenueSwitcher.tsx` pushed to the client | high | mitigate | Both must stay Server Components; asserted per file. Any new interactive leaf is extracted into its own client component, following the switcher's existing server-then-client split. |
| T-01.1-36 | Denial of Service | The create-venue call to action wrapped in a conditional | high | mitigate | A source-structural test parses the layout with the TypeScript compiler and walks the element's ancestors. Its table already covers two call sites because the defect shipped twice; the test is run per task rather than once at the end. |
| T-01.1-37 | Tampering | Native selects swapped for a styled listbox | medium | mitigate | Both native controls are retained and asserted by count, and the absence of a registry-select import is asserted. Swapping would degrade one-handed use and change an existing test's meaning. |
| T-01.1-38 | Repudiation | The language-checkbox defect silently "fixed" mid-re-skin | medium | mitigate | The block is left byte-identical, asserted by a `git diff` gate. Fixing it here would make every later red ambiguous between the fix and the re-skin; plan 01.1-13 owns it with its own regression test. |
</threat_model>

## Artifacts this phase produces

This plan creates **no new symbol**. It modifies nine pre-existing files at the layout and composition
level, routes their glyphs through `Icon`, and replaces four hardcoded string defaults in
`components/venue-form.tsx` with reads of `COPY.venues.createFirstHeading`, `COPY.venues.createFirstBody`,
`COPY.venues.createAnotherHeading` and `COPY.venues.createAnotherBody`.

Consumed from earlier plans: `Icon` (plan 01.1-07); the re-skinned primitives (plans 01.1-05, 01.1-08);
the venue Copywriting Contract rows (plan 01.1-03).
